Machine translation on a personal computer has to balance model quality, startup time, and memory. A useful service should answer a short sentence quickly, then stay responsive when several pages are translated at once. The model files stay on disk until the first request, after which the engine should reuse them instead of parsing the whole package again.

A benchmark is only comparable when both programs translate the same text, with caching disabled, on the same machine. Otherwise a fast result may only mean that one side returned a stored answer.
